column3: “On a horn of a son of oil” is rendered “on a fertile hill.”
“Grapes … wild grapes” is rendered “good grapes … worthless ones.”
NASB supplies “that” clauses (“that they may pursue,” “that wine may inflame them”).
“It will be harp and lyre … their feast” is rendered “their banquets are accompanied by.”
“Will go into exile” is rendered in the present, “go into exile”; “men of hunger” as “famished.”
“Ruins of fatlings” is rendered “waste places of the wealthy.”
“Sinks down” is rendered “collapses,” and NASB adds “blow away.”
“Like the lion” is rendered “like a lioness.”
“Someone will look” is rendered “If one looks”; NASB adds “Even.”
